mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average compresses discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines over the past 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 7.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 7.5%, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a contraction in consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline from the prior month, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 2.5%), the Federal Reserve's policy stance reduces liquidity and increases risk-free rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5%, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates strengthening manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO rises from the prior month, S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation that may prompt aggressive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 2.5%, S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises from the prior month, S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 quarterly growth rate > 2.0%), strong economic momentum supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 quarterly growth exceeds 2.0%, S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of such instances.
